summary: Indiana is permissive for the roof rat. The DNR Wild Animal Possession Permit (312 IAC 9-11) applies only to enumerated Class I/II/III animals — bears, big cats, native furbearers, venomous reptiles, etc. — none of which include rats or the genus Rattus, and DNR's permit authority reaches only protected-native or harmful/dangerous wildlife. The roof rat is also off the exotic-mammal and invasive-vertebrate lists. So keeping, breeding, and selling/giving are legal with no state permit (Indiana's commercial-breeder law is dog-only), and import needs no mandated pet-rodent CVI (rodents aren't a listed entry species) — though confirming with the Board of Animal Health is prudent. Never release one.

keep.why: The DNR Wild Animal Possession Permit scheme (312 IAC 9-11) applies only to the exhaustively enumerated Class I/II/III lists, which include no rats/Rattus; the authority (IC 14-22-26-3) reaches only protected-native or harmful/dangerous wildlife, and R. rattus is a non-native species Indiana neither protects nor lists as dangerous. It's also absent from the exotic-mammal rule (312 IAC 9-3-18.5) and invasive-vertebrate bans. No permit to keep one.

breed.why: Because keeping is unregulated by DNR, breeding is too (no possession permit attaches to a non-listed pet rodent). Indiana's only commercial-breeder statute (IC 15-21) is dogs-only. No state breeding license for pet rats.

sell_give.why: No Indiana statute licenses or restricts selling pet rodents; the exotic/wild-animal sale rules don't list Rattus, and dealer/breeder registration (IC 15-21) is dogs-only. A seller of pet roof rats is not a regulated 'animal dealer' under state law (federal USDA/AWA can apply to some commercial dealers).

transport.why: In-state transport is unrestricted. The Board of Animal Health imposes entry CVI requirements only on enumerated species (livestock, poultry, dogs/cats/ferrets) — pet rodents aren't listed, so no CVI is mandated to bring a pet rat into Indiana; confirm with BOAH before interstate movement. Never release a non-native rodent.
transport.governing_law: Indiana BOAH Entry Health Requirements (IC 15-17 authority); 312 IAC 9-11 (inapplicable).

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat — it's a non-native species; rehome responsibly. Local city/county ordinances may add limits — check yours.
